title: Three Months and One Short Stamp
subtitle: 战争和平 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 战争和平（历史社会与文化·战争与和平）
meta: 主题语境：战争和平（历史社会与文化·战争与和平）　|　核心词汇：spy　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 spy 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1968 the clerk ① caught the spy that no applicant in the office would have counted, and he said the catching was the whole of the month. The ② spy, meaning the agent itself and not the stamp, ran three months and stayed uncounted in the book; a spy, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ spy in that office had the same short stamp beside it, and the ④ spy at the far counter, meaning the form they kept for the children to sign and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A spy, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the clerk said the counting is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the spy was the whole of the matter, meaning the secret and not the agent. The ⑥ spy, meaning the secret and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; spy, he said, is either something you catch or the only word that means both an agent and a secret. He said the secret is the part they remember.

By 1973 the ⑦ spy had become a line in a file, and the file had become an argument about the short stamp. The ⑧ spy of the whole thing, the clerk wrote in May, was one office and three months of counting; spy, he said, is either the form at the far counter or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ spy I remember is the agent counted in the file, which closed in 1975 and is still counted as the quietest in the office. A ⑩ spy, my mother said in 1977, is the only agent that improves by being counted; every spy, she said, is a secret that has agreed to look like an agent. She said the secret was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 间谍（指办事处里每一名旁边的那一名）
B. n. 间谍（指那名间谍本身，与小小的印章相对）
C. 固定搭配：catch the spy 揪出这一名间谍
D. n. 间谍（指留给孩子们签的那一份）
E. n. 间谍之事（抽象总称，指一处办事处的间谍之事）
F. n. 间谍（指卷宗里写到、被清点的那一名）
G. n. 间谍、隐情（指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 隐情（抽象总称，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: caught the spy that no applicant in the office would have counted
The spy, meaning the agent itself and not the stamp
the spy at the far counter
the spy was the whole of the matter
the spy had become a line in a file
The spy of the whole thing
A spy, my mother said in 1977

answers.why: catch the spy 意为“揪出这一名间谍”，1968 年那位书记员把办事处里没有一位申请人肯清点的一名间谍做了一遍。
spy 意为“间谍”，指那名间谍本身而不是小小的印章，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被清点。
spy 意为“间谍”，指办事处里每一名旁边的那一名，每一名旁边都有同一枚小小的印章。
spy 意为“间谍”，指最远那个窗口的留给孩子们签的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
spy 意为“间谍、隐情”，指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这名隐情就是那件事的全部。
spy 意为“隐情”，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西而不是那名间谍，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
spy 意为“间谍”，指卷宗里写到、被清点的那一名，到 1973 年这一名成了卷宗里的一行。
spy 意为“间谍之事”，书记员五月写道，整件事的间谍之事是一处办事处和三个月份的清点。
spy 意为“间谍”，我记得的是卷宗里清点过的那一名，1975 年办结了，至今仍被说成办事处里最安静的一名。
spy 为抽象总称，母亲 1977 年说，间谍是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的间谍。
